articles.title: Gen Z Sports Fandom + The Mega-Moment
articles.summary: Gen Z sports fandom is shaped by culture and content, not just competition. 49% have discovered a new sport or athlete through fan-created content or off-field moments. Viral videos were the top trigger at 25%, followed by movies and TV at 23%. Fandom is also fragmented, with 48% falling into a “New Bandwagon” group that follows athletes or social content without being die-hard fans. Meanwhile, 92% of Gen Z sports fans use their phones while watching games, underscoring the importance of content beyond the live competition.

articles.title: The risk of monetizing trust: What AI advertising could get wrong
articles.summary: Every ad platform eventually monetizes the attention it gathers, but conversational AI is different because it runs on trust rather than discovery. A recommendation delivered inside an ongoing, personal dialogue reads as advice rather than an ad, so a paid placement blended into that dialogue risks eroding the confidence that makes the format work. Credibility built through expertise and strong reviews may end up mattering more than paid placement once that tension surfaces. AI advertising becomes valuable or corrosive depending on how thoughtfully the industry handles that distinction.

articles.title: How to turn first purchases into repeat orders
articles.summary: For replenishable brands, build the post-purchase journey around repeat purchase timing. Use days 1-14 to reinforce product usage, set expectations, and help customers build habits. Use days 14-21 for check-ins, results guidance, and social proof. Trigger replenishment reminders around the product's actual usage cycle with one-click reordering or subscription offers. If customers still haven't reordered after 30 days, escalate with incentives or stronger social proof.

articles.title: You should be running content experiments
articles.summary: Use TikTok to test content variables before scaling them, since duplicate posts can be tested with different text hooks, verbal openings, or higher posting volume. Use Instagram Trial Reels to test multiple versions of an idea with non-followers, then move the best performer to the main feed. For bigger content ideas, micro-test the concept on Stories, Notes, or similar low-lift channels before investing in production. Track each variable against the brand's own performance baseline to identify repeatable winners.

articles.title: The A/B Testing Framework We Use for Ecommerce
articles.summary: A strong ecommerce A/B testing program should build cumulative customer knowledge instead of treating each test as an isolated win or loss. The framework recommends tagging tests across eight purposes, such as Brand, Product Detail, Price & Value, and Usability, then using results to decide which areas deserve more testing. Replace predictions with questions to reduce bias and produce more useful learning from each test. Track funnel metrics, segment results, and define a specific follow-up test so each experiment informs the next one.

articles.title: Evolve your marketing with new AI tools
articles.summary: Google is adding AI agents across Google Ads and Google Analytics to help spot performance changes, interpret data, and act faster. New AI Overviews summarize important account updates, while personalized insight cards surface trends such as changes in demand and competitor impact. New text-prompted dashboards turn raw campaign data into visual reports and explain the reasons behind performance, and include benchmarking against anonymized averages from similar businesses.

articles.title: New Opportunities to Earn and Changes to the YouTube Partner Program
articles.summary: YouTube's raising the bar for creators to enter its monetization program starting February 1. It will require 8,000 watch hours or 20M Shorts views, up from the current thresholds. Existing Partner Program members won't be affected, but Shorts creators must maintain 10M views every 90 days to keep earning from the Shorts Creators Pool. YouTube is also expanding Premium Lite globally, giving creators another source of subscription revenue.

articles.title: Owned Media Is Not A Newsletter. It's An Operating Strategy
articles.summary: Owned media is more than launching a newsletter. It requires a clear editorial focus, original content, distribution across multiple channels, and measurement tied to audience quality. Newsletters can serve as a direct audience channel, but they're only one part of a broader system designed to build an audience around content the brand controls.

articles.title: AI-written reviews are more extreme
articles.summary: AI does not just make reviews easier to write - it changes what they say. A comparison of 117,816 hotel reviews written with and without ChatGPT access during a four-week ban in Italy in April 2023 showed a 2% rise in review volume and a 9% rise in length once AI was available, alongside a clear shift in tone. Extremely negative reviews written with AI grew harsher and more subjective rather than factual, since AI reframes ordinary complaints into stronger language than the experience itself warranted.

articles.title: How to Fight Clickbait: Meta, LinkedIn, & YouTube Case Studies
articles.summary: Feed ranking is quietly moving from rewarding what gets clicked to rewarding what a post is actually about, and the three largest platforms landed on three different architectures for it. LinkedIn replaced five separate retrieval systems with a single language-model dual encoder that serves its whole feed through nearest-neighbor search. Meta went the other way on Instagram, keeping over a thousand specialized models in a staged funnel so engagement, diversity, and integrity stay independently tunable. YouTube's PLUM system skips a search index entirely, generating a video's identifier straight from a language model.

articles.title: A 67% Majority of Creators Earn Less Than $10,000 per Year
articles.summary: Earnings track follower count and view totals more closely than engagement rate, contradicting a year of industry advice that engagement matters more than audience size.
